newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Public hold on to Tractebel stock -SGB.
newsitem.headline: Public hold on to Tractebel stock -SGB.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) said on Tuesday it expected retail investors not to respond to its offer to buy all outstanding shares in utility company Tractebel.
"Since we think investors have common sense, we consider the risk that they would sell their shares to us to be zero," chief executive officer Etienne Davignon told a news conference.
At the gathering he announced SGB's purchase of a 24.47 percent stake in Tractebel from companies in rival Belgian holding Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA GBL at a cost of 49 billion francs.
The purchase from GBL will raise SGB's stake in Tractebel to 65 percent from 40.5 percent.

SGB is also launching a bid for the remaining shares held by the public, but is offering shareholders who do not take it up on the offer a put warrant entitling them to sell their Tractebel shares to SGB at 14,500 francs each in three years' time.
The exercise price in the warrant matches that of the public offer and the price GBL is paying.
The 35 percent stake SGB does not as yet own -- 4,729,734 shares -- is worth 68.5 billion francs at the 14,500 price.
If the public were to sell all its shares to SGB, the operation would come to a total cost for SGB of 117 billion Belgian francs.
